claims.text: In the authorization code flow the browser is sent to the authorization endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri and scope; after the user authenticates, the server redirects the browser to redirect_uri with a code in the query.
The authorization code is short-lived and single-use: the client must not use it more than once, and the authorization server must deny a second use.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §4.1.2 (code MUST expire shortly after issued; MUST NOT be used more than once)

claims.text: The client exchanges the code with a POST to the token endpoint (grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id, plus code_verifier with PKCE); the tokens come back in the JSON body of that response, not in a redirect URL.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §4.1.3 Access Token Request, §4.1.4 Access Token Response; RFC 7636 §4.5; oauth-code-flow.sh:38-42; DonHang.App lib/auth/keycloak_sign_in.dart finish()

claims.text: Keycloak redirects only to a redirect_uri registered for the client; for an unregistered one it shows an error page 'Invalid parameter: redirect_uri' with status 400 instead of redirecting (oauth-code-flow.sh step 5).
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Admin Guide: OIDC clients, Valid redirect URIs; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/oauth-code-flow.txt step 5

claims.text: A client running in the browser is a public client: it cannot keep a client secret confidential, because its code is delivered to and readable by every user.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §2.1 Client Types (public clients, user-agent-based applications)

claims.text: donhang-app in keycloak/donhang-realm.json: publicClient true (no client secret), standardFlowEnabled true, implicitFlowEnabled false, one redirect URI (port 8081, /auth/callback), attribute pkce.code.challenge.method S256.

PKCE S256: the client creates a random code_verifier and sends code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) (no padding) with code_challenge_method=S256 in the authorization request; challenge_of in the script computes exactly this.

At the token endpoint the server transforms the received code_verifier with the method and compares it with the stored code_challenge; tokens are issued only if they match; Keycloak answers a mismatch with invalid_grant 'PKCE verification failed: Code mismatch'.
The SHA-256 hash in code_challenge cannot be reversed to obtain the code_verifier, so an attacker who sees the challenge or steals the code cannot produce the verifier.

With pkce.code.challenge.method set on the client, Keycloak rejects an authorization request without code_challenge: it redirects with error=invalid_request 'Missing parameter: code_challenge_method' (script step 4).
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Admin Guide: client advanced settings, Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/oauth-code-flow.txt step 4

claims.text: A scope limits what the token may be used for; DonHang.App and the script request scope=openid; Keycloak adds the client's default client scopes from donhang-realm.json, and only email and profile appear in the token response scope.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §3.3 Access Token Scope; Keycloak Server Admin Guide: Client scopes (default client scopes); donhang-realm.json:32; oauth-code-flow.txt step 2

claims.text: PKCE does not encrypt tokens; the token response is ordinary JSON over the same channel; PKCE only binds the code exchange to the client that started the flow.

oauth-code-flow.sh runs in the lab container (lab-run.sh); log_in fetches the login page, sed extracts the form action, curl prints the redirect without following it; the script cuts the token to 20 chars; code and session_state are masked only in the captured output.
response_type=code in the authorization request asks for an authorization code (as opposed to a token directly).
An authorization code travels in a browser redirect, so it shows in the address bar and can end up in the browser's history, where others may see it.
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §10.5 Authorization Codes (disclosure through user-agent history and referrer)

claims.text: PKCE uses a new code_verifier for each authorization request, so each sign-in has its own secret; the script calls new_verifier per sign-in.
claims.source_hint: RFC 7636 §4.1 (verifier created for each authorization request); oauth-code-flow.sh:44,59
